thread:
emily.nguyen: Morning all  quick async standup for provisioning. Yesterday: validated prewarm in us-west2 (2 nodes healthy), bumped ml-worker autoscaler min 2->3 to keep warm capacity, and landed a small fix to the provisioning job (PR: https://git.redwood/services/provisioning/pull/487). Noticed a brief 2x request burst from a client test around 02:10 PDT.

emily.nguyen: Blockers: us-east1 GPU quota still shows 0 for vGPU allocations after the migration to project redwood-prod-us. I opened a support ticket but no TAM reply yet. Also seeing p99 tail on inputs >1024 tokens creep up ~100ms.

raj.patel: Ack. I can escalate the cloud ticket. Can you drop the console project id and the quota metric name?

emily.nguyen: proj-9243 (redwood-prod-us). Console metric: "Accelerator GPUs (all)". Case# 202603-8812. Screenshot uploaded to the case.

chen.li: Regarding tail latency, I reproduced in staging with new kernels. Reducing batch_size for long sequences from 16 -> 8 cuts p99 by ~110-130ms. Pushed a canary config: {
  "route": "long-seq",
  "batch_size": 8,
  "kernel_hint": "fast-attn-v2"
}

priya.k: FYI: us-west2 spot pool experienced a short drain yesterday; I rescheduled lower-priority jobs onto dedicated nodes. Current p3 utilization in us-west2: 78%. us-east1 shows 96% reserved and 0 allocatable due to quota, leading to enqueues.

ops-bot: auto-scrub: fleet_health(us-west2) = OK; fleet_health(us-east1) = ALERT (nodes_available=0, enqueued_requests=14). Incident created: INC-2026-03-11-74.

raj.patel: Proposed mitigation: if quota not restored quickly, temporarily route non-critical us-east1 traffic to eu-west1 for up to 3 hours. Thoughts on latency impact?

emily.nguyen: For tier-1 customers we must avoid cross-region if p90 worsens by >150ms. Limit fallback to non-critical routes only and annotate which routes are affected in Console.

chen.li: I added a policy check in the router: allow_cross_region_fallback only if p90_estimate + cross_region_penalty < 150ms. Policy PR: https://git.redwood/policies/fallback/pull/92

priya.k: If quota remains unresolved >4h we should enable spot-fallback for low-priority queues and requeue jobs. I can flip that at 11:15 PDT unless someone objects.

emily.nguyen: OK for me. Raj, please confirm TAM ping; if quota shows up before 11:15 we abort the spot-fallback.

raj.patel: TAM contacted. Support requested quota justification; I uploaded the doc. ETA from TAM: 6-12 hours.

chen.li: Heads-up: don't start long-seq loadtests for the next 30 minutes while canary kernel rollout finishes.

dev-scheduler: notice: scheduled long-seq loadtests paused between 15:30-16:00 PDT per request.

deploy-bot: deploy: provisioning-service v3.14.2 -> v3.14.3 deployed to canary at 2026-03-11T15:20:13Z by emily.nguyen :rocket:

ops-bot: reminder: annotate any customer-impacting fallback on INC-2026-03-11-74. Use: /inc annotate <reason> <start_ts> <expected_end_ts>.

priya.k: copy. I'll annotate when I flip spot-fallback (if required).

emily.nguyen: Thanks all  I'll post a short incident summary in #incidents if quota isn't resolved in 2h. If you see enqueue spikes tag @emily.nguyen and I'll check Console.

raj.patel: updated: support acknowledged case and requested justification doc which is uploaded. Monitoring for updates.

chen.li: Quick check: anyone currently running long-seq loadtests? If so, pause for 30m until kernels finish rolling.

emily.nguyen: wrapping up this pulse. Will update thread with TAM reply or any change to fallback plan.
